title: MAGIC ENGLISH BEGINNER — WORLD 9: A2 COMMUNICATION & INDEPENDENCE
description: A high-density A2 world that moves learners from guided beginner English toward independent everyday communication, with richer grammar, longer texts, practical scenarios, problem solving and sustained speaking.

missions.title: A2 Vocabulary Expansion Lab
missions.focus: common A2 collocations, phrasal-style everyday expressions, opposites, word families and useful chunks

missions.title: People, Places & Experiences
missions.focus: describing people and places with detail, relative-style descriptive phrases and reasons

missions.title: Grammar Control Center
missions.focus: present, past and future forms in connected communication

missions.title: Questions That Keep a Conversation Going
missions.focus: follow-up questions, question words, indirect-style polite questions and clarification

missions.title: Rules, Advice & Possibility
missions.focus: must, have to, don't have to, should, can, could and may for everyday meaning

missions.title: Money, Prices & Everyday Decisions
missions.focus: budgeting vocabulary, prices, quantities, choices, preferences and simple reasons

missions.title: Home, Neighborhood & Community
missions.focus: housing, services, neighborhood descriptions, local facilities and practical questions

missions.title: Appointments & Phone English
missions.focus: making, changing and confirming appointments; leaving messages; spelling and checking information

missions.title: Customer Service Mission
missions.focus: asking for information, explaining a problem, requesting a solution and responding politely

missions.title: A2 Conversation Lab — Seven Minutes
missions.focus: sustained conversation using questions, follow-ups, opinions, experiences and future plans

missions.title: Reading Mission — A New School Project
missions.focus: 550–650 word informational/story text, main idea, details, sequence, vocabulary in context and inference

missions.title: Listening Mission — Real-World Voices
missions.focus: 5–7 minute A2 listening with announcements, conversations and short interviews

missions.title: Writing Mission — Messages That Work
missions.focus: practical emails/messages, requests, invitations, apologies, explanations and confirmations

missions.title: Storytelling Mission — A Problem and a Solution
missions.focus: 220–260 word story with setting, problem, events, solution and personal reaction

missions.title: Travel Planner
missions.focus: planning a short trip, comparing options, schedules, transport, accommodation and simple contingencies

missions.title: Emergency & Safety English
missions.focus: clear safety instructions, describing what happened, asking for urgent help and giving essential information

missions.title: Tell Me What You Think
missions.focus: opinions, preferences, reasons, agreement/disagreement and simple advantages/disadvantages

missions.title: Communication Repair Challenge
missions.focus: misunderstandings, repetition, slower speech, paraphrasing, examples and confirmation checks

missions.title: A2 Independence Marathon
missions.focus: integrated assessment requiring independent choices across vocabulary, grammar, reading, listening, speaking and writing

missions.title: WORLD 9 FINAL MASTER QUEST — A2 INDEPENDENT ENGLISH
missions.focus: multi-stage real-life quest with travel, phone, customer service, safety, reading, listening, writing and sustained speaking

content_targets.reading: 550–650 word A2 texts with main idea, detail, sequence, context vocabulary and simple inference
content_targets.listening: 5–7 minute A2 listening using announcements, conversations and short interviews
content_targets.speaking: 7-minute sustained conversation with follow-up questions, opinions, experiences and plans
content_targets.writing: 220–260 word stories plus practical messages and short emails
content_targets.mastery: Learner can participate in familiar everyday conversations with increasing independence, explain simple problems and needs, understand the main information in ordinary speech, read longer familiar texts, write connected practical messages and stories, and keep a conversation going with follow-up questions.
